correctness.rationale: With a,A coprime, A>a and parameters z∈C[[t]], valuations of x=z^a and y=z^A are aq and Aq. The minimum differential valuation is (a-1)q and the normalized one-dimensional ball volume is c_a L^{-a ceil(m/a)}, c_a=(1-L^-1)/(1-L^-a). In the product, nonzero 2×2 Jacobian minors pick one differential from each independent parameter block; their minimum order adds. The canonical product volume therefore factors at EACH fixed radius, not after averaging. The synchronized LCM period and Chinese-remainder residues grouped by d=gcd(a,b) give Theta_2=d/(ab) sum_{s=0}^{d-1}theta_d(s)^2; a geometric sum simplifies to d/(ab)*(L-1)/(L+1)*(L^d+1)/(L^d-1). For d=1 this is 1/(ab), for d>1 Hodge–Deligne rational realization distinguishes it (limit L→∞ is d). The two-cusp case equals (L²+1)/(2(L+1)²) with defect (L-1)²/[4(L+1)²]. Independent exact Fraction period averages at L=3 agree for 5 exponent pairs including gcd1 and gcd>1. Finite tests do not replace the all-exponent CRT proof; the result is restricted to the embedded definable-set density, not the intrinsic isolated-singularity formula.

The gcd-dependent correction gives an exact, explicitly nonmultiplicative pair of ordinary cusps, a meaningful boundary between coprime and resonant singular multiplicities; not a mere substitution into an already known product law.
